name: Biomedical Data Science (PhD)

rules.name: Core Biomedical Data Science Courses (12 units)
rules.notes:
Students are expected to complete the core offerings in biomedical data science. These courses should be taken for a grade, when letter grades are offered.
If the student has already completed a course covering this material in BMDS 215, BMDS 218 should be taken to fulfill this requirement.

rules.name: Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics & Engineering (21 units)
rules.notes:
• No more than nine units in courses numbered 100-199, and the rest should be 200 or above

• CS 106A Programming Methodology and CS 106B Programming Abstractions cannot be counted for this requirement

• All courses should be formal classroom-based courses, not research units

• Up to eight units of this portion of the core curriculum may be taken on a Satisfactory/No Credit basis

children.name: CS/Stats/Math/Eng courses (21 units, including the required courses)
children.desc:
To achieve in-depth mastery, PhD students are expected to create a program of study with graduate-level courses in computer science, statistics, and other technical informatics-related disciplines. The program of study may focus on aspects of these disciplines, including machine learning, statistical modeling, artificial intelligence, data mining, image analysis, human-computer interaction, and data visualization.
In addition to the 10-13 units students will earn through the Required Courses listed above, students should also choose courses from the electives list below to reach the total of 21 units needed for this requirement.
children.notes: Crosslisted offerings for any of the courses listed above are accepted in place of the offering listed.

rules.name: Social and Ethical Issues (4 units)
rules.desc: Students should take MED 255. The Responsible Conduct of Research in their first year.
rules.notes: Students are expected to be familiar with issues regarding responsible conduct of research, reproducibility of research, and ethical, legal, social, organizational, and behavioral aspects of the impact of biomedical informatics technologies on society. Courses that fulfill this requirement can be found by entering “dbds::ethics” in the Explore Courses search box. These courses may be taken on a Satisfactory/No credit basis.

children.name: Social and Ethical Issues courses (4 units, MED 255 included)

rules.name: Domain Biology or Medicine (6 units)
rules.desc:
Students should take classes relevant to their application area interests. The core curriculum and domain biology/medicine requirements should be completed by the end of the second year of graduate study. Classes on the following list are pre-approved. Other classes can be used to fulfill this requirement with department approval.
Domain Biology courses can be taken as Credit/No Credit (CR/NC).

rules.name: Thesis Pre-Proposal Seminar
rules.desc: During the third year of training, each doctoral student must give a thesis pre-proposal seminar that describes evolving research plans.

rules.name: At least two research rotations in the first year
Regular participation in the student seminar (BMDS 201A-C) and a research colloquium
Teaching Assistantship
rules.desc: Each student must be a teaching assistant for two courses as assigned by the Biomedical Data Science Executive Committee; one should be completed in the first two years of study. Students may register for up to three BMDS 295 Biomedical Informatics Teaching Methods units to obtain credit for each teaching assistantship.

rules.name: Advancement to candidacy

children.name: Qualifying exam by the end of the second year
Application for candidacy by the beginning of the third year

rules.desc: After applying for Terminal Graduate Registration (TGR) status and completing 135 units, the PhD candidate should register each quarter for BIOMEDIN 802 TGR PhD Dissertation so that their research effort may be counted toward the degree.

rules.name: Oral Exam
rules.desc:
Each student must present and defend their dissertation work before a University Oral Examination Committee that includes at least one member of the DBDS Faculty. The committee determines whether the student’s general knowledge of the field and the details of their completed research are sufficient to be granted the doctoral degree. Further information about the Oral Examination and the submission of the written dissertation is in the DBDS Student Handbook and university policies cited therein.
The student is expected to demonstrate an ability to present scholarly material and research in a lecture at a formal seminar.

rules.name: Dissertation

children.name: Dissertation advisor from the DBDS faculty (or approved)
Paper suitable for a refereed journal, approved by the advisor
Dissertation accepted by the reading committee

rules.desc:
The most important requirement for the PhD degree is the dissertation. Each student must secure the agreement of a member of the DBDS faculty to act as the doctoral dissertation advisor or obtain departmental approval for a dissertation advisor to be appointed from outside the major department. This approval will depend on research rationale, potential advisor’s commitment to program’s rules, and identification of a DBDS faculty to participate in the thesis committee. See DBDS Student Handbook for details.
After applying for Terminal Graduate Registration (TGR) status and completing 135 units, the PhD candidate should register each quarter for BMDS 802 TGR PhD Dissertation so that their research effort may be counted toward the degree.
Each student must present and defend their dissertation work before a University Oral Examination Committee that includes at least one member of the DBDS faculty. The committee determines whether the student’s general knowledge of the field and the details of their completed research are sufficient to be granted the doctoral degree. Further information about the Oral Examination and the submission of the written dissertation is in the DBDS Student Handbook and university policies cited therein.
The student is expected to demonstrate an ability to present scholarly material and research in a lecture at a formal seminar.
The student is expected to demonstrate an ability to present scholarly material in concise written form. Each student must write a paper suitable for publication, usually discussing their doctoral research project. The student’s advisor must approve this paper as suitable for submission to a refereed journal before the department confers the doctoral degree.
The dissertation must be accepted by a doctoral dissertation reading committee composed of the principal dissertation advisor and two other readers. A fourth reader may be added at the discretion of the student and the principal advisor.

gpa: A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or greater to remain in good academic standing.
policies:
The PhD program requires 135 units; 43 of those units should be formal coursework (classroom-based courses, not research units).
In the first year, at least two research rotations are required.
Doctoral students generally advance to PhD candidacy after passing the qualifying exam, which takes place by the end of the second year of training. A student’s academic advisor is primarily responsible for the program’s adequacy, which the Biomedical Data Science Executive Committee regularly reviews. The student must fulfill these requirements and apply for admission to candidacy for the PhD by the beginning of the third year.
During the third year of training, each doctoral student must give a thesis pre-proposal seminar that describes evolving research plans.
Students are expected to participate regularly in the Biomedical Data Science Student Seminar and a research colloquium which is listed as BMDS 201A, B and C in fall/winter/spring quarters. Regardless of their enrollment, they should attend all meetings throughout their graduate training and a research colloquium appropriate to their interests.
transferPolicy: Students who completed graduate coursework at another institution are encouraged to transfer course units in winter quarter of their first year of doctoral study. Up to 24 transfer units are allowable from other graduate programs. The Director of Graduate Studies will evaluate the transfer of units on a course-by-course basis. Graduate work accepted for transfer of residency does not automatically exempt a student from having to complete a course requirement for the degree. University policies related to the transfer of credit for graduate work done elsewhere can be found here.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 12 letter-graded units of core courses, 21 units of CS, statistics, math and engineering including CS 161, STATS 200 and STATS 315A or CS 229 (at most 9 units numbered 100-199, and at most 8 units taken S/NC), 4 units of social and ethical issues including MED 255, 6 units of domain biology or medicine, and 135 graduate units. The 3.0 GPA, two research rotations in the first year, regular seminar and colloquium attendance, the thesis pre-proposal seminar, two TA assignments, the qualifying exam by the end of the second year, candidacy, the oral exam, a publishable paper and the dissertation are checked by hand.
